discussion_comments.comment_body:
**maintainer-decision** This flips the Up-arrow default from global to `session`, which is a user-visible default-behavior change and the crux of the whole PR. Two things for @can1357 to weigh in on before this merges:

1. Issue #4331 is labeled `enhancement` and every comment in the thread (including the prior roboomp triage comments) explicitly holds for maintainer sign-off that never came — this is the first code on it.
2. The default chosen here (`session`) deviates from the converged proposal in the issue, which was **repo-scoped** Up-arrow by default (roboomp's proposal, backed by @Mathews-Tom). @wernerbisschoff/@gioknx argued for `session`; the two are genuinely in tension for parallel-session-in-one-repo users.

Everything downstream (`repo` resolution, `searchScope` default `global`, unscoped `matchingSessionIds`) matches the converged design; only this default value is the open call. Not a code defect — flagging so the default is a conscious maintainer decision, not an implicit one.

Addressed in `dee751a04a`: the default is back to `global`, so this PR changes no default behavior — narrowing the scope is opt-in through `history.scope`. The schema description, `docs/settings.md`, `docs/keybindings.md`, both CHANGELOG entries and the PR body were updated to match. The `session`-vs-`repo` default is left to the maintainer as a follow-up choice; both are reachable today by setting the key, and `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` work unconfigured inside `Ctrl+R`.

**blocking** — This registers a third-party `capability` binary (from the external capability-replicas/agentmux project, not this repo) as a default MCP server for every user who has something named `capability` on PATH, with `timeout: 0` (line 96) so its requests never time out. Combined with the deletion of `src/tools/wait.ts`, core async-job semantics (`task`/`bash` background, `irc`, services) now depend on an out-of-tree CLI whose tool name (`agentmux_capability_wait`, line 63) is pinned to that project's internal namespacing. This is an architectural/default-behavior change that needs its own PR and explicit maintainer sign-off; it is unrelated to the SQL-sessions title.

**should-fix** — `SqlSessionStorage.create({ client })` drops the table override, so `SESSIONS_DB_TABLE` is ignored even though the header (line 13) and the dry-run output (line 170) say it applies. The importer writes to `omp_session_files` while a live run with `SESSIONS_DB_TABLE` set reads a different table. It also skips `OMP_SESSION_PATH_PREFIX_ALIAS`: run on the aliased machine, it keys rows under `/home/...` and splits them from the canonical `/Users/...` rows. Reusing `resolveSessionStorage()` (or passing `table`/`pathAlias`) fixes both.

**should-fix (silent fallback outside tasks):** `isolation.backend` isn't task-only. `session-worktree.ts:153`, `tools/gh-pr-checkout.ts:502` and `cli/worktree-cli.ts:153` all pass `parseIsolationBackend(cfgIsolationBackend.get(settings))`. With `"command"` they get `undefined` and silently use `auto`, without running `isolation.command`. That's the silent PAL fallback the PR contract says it avoids. Either reject `"command"` on those paths with a clear error, or document in the setting description and `docs/tools/task.md` that it applies only to `isolated: true` task spawns. Moving the command toggle out of the shared enum would also work, e.g. a non-empty `isolation.command` selects the mode.

Documented rather than rejected: the `command` option description and the `isolation.command` setting description now state "Task spawns only — other worktree consumers treat `command` as `auto`". A non-empty-command-selects-mode refactor would be a larger API change; happy to do it if the maintainer prefers that shape.

**Blocking:** `expandMCPServerEnv()` suppresses an unresolved `args`/`command` reference whenever its name occurs in the server's `env`, but `resolveStdioSpawnCommand()` passes `config.args` directly to `Bun.spawn` (`transports/stdio.ts:341-342,610`). Only an explicitly invoked shell expands those values. For `{ command: "bun", args: ["--token=${TOKEN}"], env: { TOKEN: "secret" }`, the spawned argv still contains literal `${TOKEN}` and no `unresolvedEnv` is recorded; the new fail-fast contract silently fails. Resolve the value for direct-spawn arguments or restrict the exemption to actual shell expansion, and test the argv received by the child rather than just whether it connects.

Fixed in 8c5cb28882: own-`env` references in `command`/`args` are now substituted with the value the child receives. Process env and plugin env still win; literal keys are used verbatim; plain values resolve like connect-time env (`$envExact(v) || v`, empty counts as unset); `!command` values are replaced with the command output at connect time. The leave-literal exemption is gone. An argv-echo stdio fixture asserts the spawned child receives `--key=secret` and `--cmd=<command output>`; the discovery and connection tests fail when either half is reverted.

**blocking:** `Settings` does not runtime-validate array elements, and `omp config set` only checks `Array.isArray` (`packages/coding-agent/src/cli/config-cli.ts:203-214`). A CLI-accepted value such as `[1]` therefore reaches this callback and throws `TypeError: id.trim is not a function` before the request. Please validate/normalize every element as a string and add a malformed-element regression test; the schema cast cannot protect YAML/CLI input.

Fixed in d65ab5be: entries now pass a type guard ((id): id is string => typeof id === "string" && id.trim().length > 0), so non-string YAML/CLI elements are dropped instead of throwing before the stream starts. Regression test covers [1, "claude-opus-5", null, "  "] forwarding exactly [{model: "claude-opus-5"}].

Addressed at the current head (1280e4b0): every element is validated with a `typeof id === "string"` type guard before use, so a CLI/YAML-supplied `[1]` no longer reaches `.trim()`. Regression test covers `[1, "claude-opus-5", null, "  "]` forwarding exactly `[{ model: "claude-opus-5" }]`.

**should-fix — separate the default-on timestamp feature.** This PR claims to ship `mnemopi.facts.scope`, yet `prompt.nowStamp` defaults to true and `sdk.ts:3464,4157` now appends a new system-reminder block to provider-visible user/developer turns in every coding-agent session. That is an unrelated default prompt-behavior change across a second package (and the bulk of this 24-file diff); it needs a separate maintainer decision, not to ride with the facts schema fix. Please split the coding-agent timestamp changes out of this PR.
